reviewer: research-data author; independent final reviewer must assess the exact artifacts separately

pages.observations: Panels001–012 show an apparently single walking person at each midpoint against the same curtained space. Initial/final frames are frequently empty or contain only a partial body. Visible clothing and limb overlap limit joint-location verification.

Panels013–024 have the same entry/exit pattern. Panel020.1 is a decoded black frame, not proof of video-open failure. Midpoints generally place pose estimates on the visible walker, with some distal-point uncertainty.

Panels025–036 show one apparent walker at each midpoint. Several start/end stills show only the scene or a cropped person. Pose points follow the body coarsely, but the photographs do not validate anatomical joints.
Panels037–048 show a consistent static scene and walking person at midpoints. Some wrist/leg points are uncertain under clothing, and subjects leave the field of view at the final still.

Panels049–060 span two filming framings. The normal-sized moving person is generally visible centrally, while recording boundaries are cropped. Foot estimates sometimes cluster near or below visible foot outlines.

Panels061–072 show one apparent walker per midpoint with repeated entry/exit truncation. Raw points are broadly on the body, but marker bands and overlapping legs make precise joint assignment uncertain.
Panels073–084 show a single apparent walker per midpoint and no obvious change to a different person in the selected stills. Boundary frames frequently contain a partial or absent subject.

Panels085–093 generally show one apparent walker per midpoint. Panel094.2 and094.3 include a second person closely behind and overlapping the foreground walker. The raw pose appears on the foreground body at the selected midpoint, but the first-pose identity cannot be guaranteed through the full recording.

review_order: Inspected panel-numbered pages without source/condition labels, then unblinded flagged Panel094 using the separate ledger. Panel numbers retain deterministic participant order, so this is partial blinding rather than a clinical blinded study.

identity_risks.observation: Two overlapping people; full-image first-pose association remains uncertain.
identity_risks.recommendation: Retain the declared primary data identity and report a pre-score identity-risk sensitivity excluding this participant if the coordinator freezes it before efficacy inspection.

conclusion: The full sample reveals substantial frame-entry/exit missingness and one clear multiple-person overlap risk. Midpoint stills broadly support a walking-subject interpretation but cannot establish complete identity tracking or anatomical accuracy.
limits: Only one recording per participant and three stills per recording were viewed.
The other direction and between-still frames were not visually verified.
Clinical labels and severity were not inferred or reassessed from appearance.
The raw33-joint confidence summary is a different descriptive quantity from16-joint support and should not be used interchangeably.
